traceability.notes: The story 008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX defines a limited, well-scoped first iteration of auto-fix functionality: automatically adding missing @story annotations to functions/methods with a simple built-in template, and normalizing simple @story path suffix issues, while keeping all more complex scenarios out of scope. The current implementation satisfies this scope in full. The require-story-annotation rule exposes fixable auto-fix behavior that only inserts a placeholder @story JSDoc above functions/methods, preserving runtime code and general formatting; this behavior is thoroughly exercised by dedicated Jest RuleTester tests covering multiple node types. The valid-annotation-format rule provides fixable support strictly for safe suffix normalization of @story paths, implemented via carefully bounded range replacements and guarded by checks that limit fixes to simple, unambiguous cases. When a safe fix cannot be determined, the rule only reports errors, as required. Both rules are exported through the plugin entrypoint and thus fully integrated with ESLint’s --fix workflow. User-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md clearly explains what auto-fix does for each rule and the safety constraints, explicitly referencing Story 008.0. Requirements explicitly flagged in the story as “Not yet implemented” (configurable templates and selective fine-grained fix toggles) are correctly left out of this iteration and are not part of the acceptance criteria. With passing dedicated tests, aligned implementation, and up-to-date documentation, this story’s implemented portion is complete and conforms to its defined acceptance criteria for the current release.
